businesses.name: Amazon Air Hub
businesses.story: The city's air hub flies parcels in and out every night. When a gate changes, crews and airlines must hear at once. Parcels need tracking, and the busy season brings far more planes. Help the hub run on AWS.
businesses.simple: A cargo airport. Planes, gates and parcels all need to stay in step, even on the busiest night.
businesses.brandNote: The Amazon Air name and livery show only when BRAND is on. Every task teaches what AWS's airport guidance says airports and airlines do; nothing here describes how Amazon Air really runs.

sources.title: Guidance for Near Real-Time Airport Gate Change Information on AWS
facts: A gate change is stored in the airport operational database; AWS DMS captures each change.
Changes go to Amazon MSK or Kinesis Data Streams; a Lambda function reshapes them and sends them to EventBridge.
EventBridge rules route events to each airline (for example, flight numbers starting with ABC go to Airline 1).
Airlines run EventBridge in their own accounts; the airport is allowed to push events there, using IAM policies for cross-account access.
Airline Lambda functions find affected passengers and notify them through Amazon SNS.
Reliability: run DMS Multi-AZ, know Lambda concurrency limits in your Region, set CloudWatch alarms; EventBridge can replay, retry and deliver to many targets.
Sustainability: Lambda can run on Arm processors.

sources.title: Guidance for Airport Data Management on AWS
facts: Systems of record: schedules, near real-time flight information, check-ins, weather, aircraft position, billing.
Baggage sortation events from bar code scanners or RFID can be ingested with AWS IoT and Amazon Kinesis.
Batch and near real-time data is staged in Amazon S3 in cost-effective storage classes.
Amazon EMR and AWS Glue transform the data; Redshift, Athena and QuickSight analyse it; SageMaker builds models for operational analytics.
DynamoDB, Lambda and API Gateway serve operational data stores and near real-time dashboards; DynamoDB Streams and Step Functions publish flight events downstream.
Security: IAM roles control people and machine access; data is encrypted in motion and at rest; customer-controlled AWS KMS keys are an option.

businesses.name: Riverside Bank
businesses.story: Riverside Bank keeps people's savings and moves their money. Customers want to sign in from their phones, payday brings a flood of card payments, and every penny must stay safe and on record. Help the bank build it on AWS.
businesses.simple: A bank. It keeps money safe, moves it fast and writes down who did what.

sources.title: Financial Services Industry Lens (AWS Well-Architected Framework)
facts: Covers paying for goods and services, markets, lending and insurance.
Best practices for security, data privacy and resiliency for financial institutions, plus transparency and auditability.

sources.title: Financial Services Industry Lens: Security
facts: Security by design: encryption for data at rest and in transit on by default, with careful control of encryption keys.
Automated governance: account management, budgets, security and compliance automation.
Generative AI: access controls across AI components, guardrails, least privilege for agents and protection against prompt injection.

sources.title: Financial Services Industry Lens: Reliability
facts: Zonal services such as EC2 and EBS fail independently in each Availability Zone; S3, SQS and DynamoDB are Regional services built across zones.
You choose whether an RDS database has a synchronous replica or runs as a standalone instance.
Payment processing is one of the workloads many industries depend on.

sources.title: Guidance for Payments Fraud Prevention on AWS
facts: Near real-time transactions go to Kinesis Data Streams; Lambda reads the stream.
API Gateway invokes Lambda functions for inference; SageMaker models score each transaction.
Fraud ring and profile analytics are stored in DynamoDB; history lands in S3, Glue runs ETL, Athena queries it.
Kinesis and Lambda scale with demand; S3 supports server-side encryption.

sources.title: AWS for Financial Services

tasks.why: A bank can't close because one building lost power. A standby in another zone takes over.

choose.question: The ledger database is ready. Should it run alone, or with a standby copy in another Availability Zone?

options.text: Multi-AZ: a synchronous standby in another zone that takes over if the first fails

options.text: One instance; backups are enough
options.why: Backups bring data back, but restoring takes time. A bank needs to keep running, not just recover later.

businesses.name: City Arena
businesses.story: City Arena hosts the big match every Saturday. Tickets sell out in minutes, fans want live stats on their phones, and bots try to grab the best seats first. Help the arena build it on AWS.
businesses.simple: A sports stadium. Ticket day is a stampede, and match day needs live stats for every fan.

sources.title: Smart Venues (AWS for Sports)
facts: Venue systems can be brought into a common data lake, with management dashboards and digital twins for near real-time operations.
Services named: Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Rekognition, AWS IoT, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon S3.

sources.title: Behind the scenes: AWS real-time architecture for Bundesliga Match Facts
facts: EventBridge Scheduler triggers a Lambda function that checks for live matches and starts the containers.
AWS Fargate runs one container per statistic per game; the article credits Fargate with a 99.9% cost reduction compared with fixed servers.
Amazon SageMaker hosts the models; S3 archives inputs and outputs; Aurora Serverless stores results for dashboards.
Over 3.6 million events per match; events must be handled within seconds.

sources.title: How to Manage Peak Traffic on AWS Using Queue-it's Virtual Waiting Room (AWS Partner Network Blog)
facts: Peak events can push site visits to 2 to 25 times normal within seconds.
A waiting room controls the rate at which visitors enter; load balancers spread requests and DDoS protection filters bad traffic, which is different.
Auto Scaling, load testing and caching are standard practice but may not cover traffic that arrives faster than capacity can be added.
The integration runs on Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge.

sources.title: Fan Engagement (AWS for Sports)
facts: Leagues and teams often lack tools to store fan data and use it for personal experiences; services named include Fargate, Lambda, Redshift and QuickSight.

sources.title: HIPAA Eligible Services Reference
facts: Listed services may be used with protected health information, subject to the shared responsibility model; customers must still configure them to meet the rules.

facts: Uploading a document to S3 triggers a Lambda function, which sends it to Amazon Textract.

Athena queries the data, QuickSight shows it, and SageMaker hosts prediction models.

facts: Providers unlock siloed data and build personalised care plans.

options.text: Any AWS service is automatically safe for patient data, set up however you like

options.text: Patient data can never go in the cloud

settings.why: Its own key lets the hospital control who can unlock records and see each use.

sources.title: Guidance for Web Store on AWS
facts: Route 53 points the shop's name at CloudFront, which caches static content from S3 and is protected by AWS WAF against common exploits and bots.
Cognito signs customers in; API Gateway exposes the backend services; an Application Load Balancer spreads traffic across Availability Zones.
Microservices run on Fargate and Lambda; DynamoDB stores products, customers and orders; DAX and ElastiCache cache results.
EventBridge lets services react to events; an SQS first-in-first-out queue sends placed orders to the order management system; OpenSearch powers product search.
Caching at several tiers cuts how often data and services are hit, which also cuts cost.

sources.title: How to plan for peak demand on an AWS serverless digital commerce platform
facts: Increase Lambda concurrency to absorb sudden spikes; shorter functions raise throughput.
Use a high-cardinality attribute such as OrderId as the DynamoDB partition key.
Use queues and streams instead of direct calls so parts don't overwhelm each other.
Graceful degradation: still show a product page if the promotions service is down; use circuit breakers.
Track business metrics such as orders per minute; use CloudWatch anomaly detection; run load tests and fault-injection experiments.

Secrets Manager protects secrets and rotates them automatically; Parameter Store keeps configuration out of the code.

businesses.name: Streaming Studio
businesses.story: The Streaming Studio makes films and shows, and now it wants to stream them to every phone, laptop and telly in town. Each new film must be turned into versions that play on every screen, sent out fast, and the old ones kept safely and cheaply. Help the studio build its streaming service on AWS.
businesses.simple: A film studio going online. Every film has to play on every screen, and nobody likes waiting for it to load.

sources.title: Video on Demand on AWS: architecture overview
facts: An S3 bucket holds the source media files; content is eventually stored in S3 Glacier according to the S3 lifecycle policy.
AWS Step Functions creates ingest, processing and publishing step functions; Lambda functions do the work of each step and process error messages.
A DynamoDB table stores data captured through the workflow.
AWS Elemental MediaConvert transcodes media files from their source format; MediaPackage (optional) formats streams to play on several devices and can encrypt content.
CloudWatch is used for logging, with CloudWatch Events rules for MediaConvert notifications; Amazon SNS topics send encoding, publishing and error notifications.
A second S3 bucket stores the destination media files; a CloudFront distribution delivers the video to end users; an SQS queue captures the workflow outputs.

sources.title: Video on Demand on AWS: solution overview
facts: The solution ingests metadata files and source videos, processes the videos for playback on a wide range of devices, stores the transcoded files and delivers them through CloudFront.
By default it can encode MP4, MPG, M4V, M2TS and MOV files.
Estimated cost in US East (N. Virginia) is USD $4.23 per month for AWS resources.

sources.title: AWS for Media & Entertainment
facts: Services listed include Amazon Bedrock (build and scale generative AI apps), Bedrock AgentCore (deploy and run AI agents), CloudFront (deliver content with low latency and high transfer speeds), Amazon S3 (object storage for any amount of data), S3 Vectors (vector storage for AI workloads at lower cost than traditional vector databases) and Amazon Interactive Video Service (live stream and interactive video).
Warner Bros. Discovery broadcast the Olympic Games on Discovery+ in Europe with a 14% total user engagement increase with Amazon Personalize.
Formula 1's Media2Cloud ingested 4PB of archived footage.

businesses.name: Game Studio
businesses.story: The Game Studio is about to launch a phone game. Nobody knows if a thousand people will play or ten million, and every day at ten o'clock a new in-game event starts and everyone logs on at once. Help the studio keep the game fast on launch day and learn what its players enjoy.
businesses.simple: A team making a phone game. Players can turn up in their millions, all at the same second.

sources.title: AWS for Games
facts: Roughly 750 million gamers each month play games built on AWS; AWS has over 16 years of games expertise and over 300 AWS Games Partners.
Epic Games' Fortnite has seen over 15.3 million concurrent players during live events and over 110 million active players.
Amazon GameLift is named in a headline: it achieves 100 million concurrently connected users per game.
A blog post covers mood board creation with Miro and Amazon Bedrock.

sources.title: Guidance for Game Analytics Pipeline on AWS
facts: A modular, serverless pipeline collects real-time and batch telemetry from game clients and backend services; it scales with usage, from early playtesting to production.
It accepts data from any HTTP/HTTPS REST source, such as game clients, game servers or backend services.
A serverless API backend using API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB authenticates and either sends events or performs administrative tasks.
An optional real-time option uses Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink and OpenSearch Service for real-time ingest, processing and dashboards.
The data lake option batches events with Amazon Data Firehose, stores them in Parquet in S3 with Hive or Iceberg tables, processes them with AWS Glue and queries them with Athena.
The data warehouse option ingests events from Kinesis Data Streams into Redshift Serverless.

sources.title: A mobile game scales to millions of players with DynamoDB (AWS Database Blog)
facts: Over 8 million people play every day of the week, more than 70% of the game's 10 million+ daily players; early traffic was more than 5 times the best-case estimates.
At peak the game drove 2.1 million writes per second to DynamoDB, which stores player accounts, inventory and friend lists.
All tables launched in on-demand mode because traffic could not be predicted; some high-traffic tables later moved to provisioned mode to save money.
On-demand tables instantly handle up to double the previous peak; for bigger events the team prewarmed tables by switching to provisioned mode with high capacity, then back to on-demand.

One table throttled when all clients wrote at exactly 10:00:00 even though the per-minute average never reached its capacity: CloudWatch averages over one minute, DynamoDB throttles over much shorter windows. They needed 20 times the capacity they had assumed; spreading writes over a longer window reduced throttling.

For matchmaking they rejected DynamoDB Streams plus Lambda materialized views because the extra writes cost too much, and chose a read-heavy design: query a player's friends, then their friends' friends in parallel.

facts: The publishing platform, an AWS Partner, provides content management and distribution for publishers; its AI suite offers summarization, automated tagging, translation and social media post generation. A French newspaper is the customer named.
Amazon Bedrock supplies the foundation models and knowledge bases; Amazon Polly is used alongside it.
An Application Load Balancer routes requests to a container in an Amazon ECS cluster, where a Python server handles them.
The server queries DynamoDB for metadata and sends prompts to Bedrock and Polly; generated videos and images are saved to S3.

sources.title: A newspaper speeds up audio narration with Amazon Polly (AWS Machine Learning Blog)
facts: The content system publishes each saved article version to an Amazon SNS topic; a subscribed Lambda function splits the article into SSML documents, roughly one per paragraph.
Each SSML document is checked against calculated hashes; only new or changed paragraphs are sent to Polly. A typo fix re-synthesizes only that paragraph.
Polly's audio fragments go to an S3 bucket; a second Lambda function, triggered by object creation, merges them; the merged file goes to a bucket that is the origin of a CloudFront distribution.
Lambda@Edge paywalls premium articles: non-subscribers hear only the first paragraph.
Synthesized characters fell by at least 50%; SZ.de reaches more than 15 million monthly unique users (October 2021); about 200 users subscribed after hearing a paywalled teaser.

sources.title: Guidance for Reading & Highlighting Web Content with Amazon Polly
facts: Polly reads a webpage aloud and highlights the text as it's narrated, which helps accessibility.
For static pages, audio is pre-generated at build time, stored in S3 and downloaded through CloudFront; a marks file drives the highlighting.
For dynamic pages, the browser uses an AWS identity from a Cognito identity pool scoped to just enough access to Polly and the S3 bucket.
CloudFront can keep visitors from reaching the bucket directly and allows signed URLs or cookies, geographic restrictions and AWS WAF; a bucket policy can require HTTPS; the bucket is encrypted.
Pre-generating speech means Polly converts text only once (synthesize once, listen many); caching helps popular audio; the Polly request character count grows with requests.

sources.title: A big port tackles supply chain challenges with AWS (AWS Public Sector Blog)
facts: The Port of Long Beach is the second-busiest port in the United States and handles more than $200 billion in cargo each year.
Its Supply Chain Information Highway gives stakeholders end-to-end visibility into cargo movement.
Incoming cargo data is stored in Amazon S3, queued in Amazon SQS, converted to a consistent format by AWS Lambda, stored back in S3, and indexed in Amazon OpenSearch Service so it can be searched.
Ocean carriers and trucking companies can build their own insights from the data; the aim is fewer delays at each handoff.
A proof of concept was built within a couple of months after a Working Backwards session.

sources.title: A port community system scales on AWS (AWS case study)
facts: Portbase runs the Dutch port community platform for more than 6,000 organisations and 26,000 users.
It runs its critical applications on a serverless, cloud-native platform on AWS that scales automatically on demand.
It can launch data dashboards quickly during disruptions such as the 2021 Suez Canal blockade.
Data owners can share data with other solution providers on their own terms.

sources.title: Guidance for Product Traceability on AWS
facts: AWS Glue ingests and cleans third-party data such as shipping and invoice information.
Suppliers upload certificates through a serverless portal built with Route 53, Cognito, CloudFront and S3.
Lifecycle rules move certificates from S3 to S3 Glacier automatically.
EventBridge starts an extraction workflow run by Step Functions; Textract reads key details such as the expiry date and certificate number.
Amazon Location Service maps supplier addresses to coordinates; extracted data can be cross-checked against third-party data.
Final data is read with Athena or Redshift; CloudWatch and CloudTrail monitor the services; AWS KMS manages encryption keys.
Security: AWS WAF, Cognito and AWS Certificate Manager protect the upload portal; all data is encrypted at rest with KMS keys.
Reliability: run extraction in Step Functions with retries, because Textract has account-level concurrency limits and calls can be throttled when many certificates arrive at once.

sources.title: Guidance for Meter Data Analytics on AWS
facts: Utilities ingest meter data and combine it with weather and map data to detect meter and circuit anomalies, thwart energy theft, predict demand and engage customers.

Amazon Timestream stores time-series data; AWS Glue and Amazon EMR process data; S3 holds raw data and archives; S3 Glacier keeps archival copies for retention.
Curated data sits in an S3 data lake with an AWS Glue Data Catalog; Athena runs one-time queries; Redshift queries petabytes with SQL.
SageMaker and Amazon Personalize detect grid anomalies and predict equipment failures; dashboards use QuickSight or Amazon Managed Grafana.
Security: the Glue Data Catalog is encrypted; design IAM roles with least privilege.
Reliability: Glue, S3 and Athena are serverless and scale with data; SNS and SQS let ingestion grow without disruption.
Operations: CloudFormation manages the infrastructure stack. Cost: serverless where possible (Lambda, Athena, Kinesis).

sources.title: AWS for Manufacturing
facts: Smart manufacturing captures and analyses plant-floor data to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness.
Volkswagen uses AWS IoT, machine learning, analytics and compute to improve plant efficiency and uptime.
Georgia-Pacific gained data insights and simpler data collection, contributing to a profit increase of millions of dollars.

sources.title: Guidance for Predictive Maintenance with Amazon Monitron
facts: Sensors on equipment and a gateway in the factory send data into Kinesis Data Streams; Kinesis Data Firehose delivers it to an S3 bucket, the foundation of an industrial data lake.
S3 notifications send events to EventBridge; a Lambda function processes each event and passes it to an AWS IoT Events state machine.
On a warning state, Lambda creates a work order and an SNS topic notifies staff by text message, mobile push and email.
A Glue job, scheduled through EventBridge, keeps the Data Catalog up to date; Athena queries the S3 data; Amazon Managed Grafana shows the results.
Security: IAM and AWS KMS manage access and encryption; CloudTrail audits. Operations: CloudFormation keeps deployments consistent; CloudWatch monitors.
Cost: S3 Intelligent-Tiering optimises storage costs for large-scale sensor data.

sources.title: Visual inspection automation using Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
facts: The Product Defect Detection solution in SageMaker JumpStart trains and deploys models that find defects on steel surfaces.
The NEU dataset has 1,800 greyscale images of hot-rolled steel strip, 300 for each of six defect types: crazing, inclusion, pitted surface, patches, rolled-in scale and scratches.
Notebooks download data from S3, train models and deploy them to a real-time SageMaker endpoint that answers over HTTPS.
CloudFormation creates the resources; CloudWatch monitors training and endpoint metrics; deleting the parent stack cleans up.

sources.title: Manufacturing execution systems on AWS: AI/ML (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)
facts: A camera on a conveyor belt or packaging station can help inspect up to 100 percent of parts.
AWS IoT Greengrass runs the anomaly check locally for latency-sensitive inspection; AWS Outposts can host compute and databases on site.
The edge part can sync with the cloud part through an Amazon API Gateway endpoint.
SageMaker AI builds and trains the model in the cloud; the trained model is deployed at the edge, which can feed data back to retrain it.
AWS Panorama reached end of support on May 31, 2026.

sources.title: Guidance for Building an Agricultural Sensor Network using IoT and Amazon DocumentDB
facts: Soil sensors and weather stations measure temperature, rainfall, soil moisture and crop conditions, and send JSON data to AWS IoT Core.
An AWS IoT rule forwards the data to Amazon MSK; a Kafka connector on AWS Fargate stores it in Amazon DocumentDB.
Containerised microservices on Amazon ECS, Fargate or Amazon EKS process sensor and third-party data and make recommendations; farmers are notified through Amazon SNS.
Amazon EventBridge triggers a Lambda function periodically to collect weather updates and soil test results from third parties.
Officers, insurers or farmers can reach the app through Amazon API Gateway; Amazon Cognito protects it; admins can report with Amazon Athena or QuickSight.
Every device or sensor needs a credential; all traffic to and from AWS IoT is encrypted with TLS; IAM roles give Lambda only the permissions it needs.
DocumentDB runs as a three-node cluster across three Availability Zones; backup is on by default and it can be restored to any second in the retention period, up to the last five minutes.
DocumentDB's flexible schema suits the changing sensors and hardware common in agricultural IoT; use CloudWatch logging for each service.

sources.title: Guidance for Fleet Management for Connected Farms on AWS
facts: Tractors and combine harvesters carry sensors and cameras; AWS IoT Greengrass runs processing and machine learning inference on the machine with Lambda, to cut the cost of sending data to the cloud.
Greengrass Stream Manager batches data during a network failure and forwards it when the connection is back.
Devices authenticate with X.509 certificates or Amazon Cognito; use IAM least privilege and rotate passwords and keys.
CloudWatch collects logs and alarms; Amazon SNS sends event notifications; AWS IoT rules report devices that have issues.

sources.title: Solutions for Agriculture
facts: Lists QnABot on AWS, a multi-channel, multi-language chatbot powered by large language models.
Lists guidance for a high-performance numerical weather prediction system and for industrial data fabrics.

sources.title: Amazon Athena DocumentDB connector
facts: The Amazon Athena DocumentDB connector lets Athena query DocumentDB data with SQL.
Deploy the connector to your account with the Athena console or the AWS Serverless Application Repository first.
By default the connector infers each collection's schema from a small number of documents; it can read the schema from the AWS Glue Data Catalog instead.

facts: Throughout its life a vehicle periodically calls an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint to get its latest configuration; each production stage needs different software configurations.
Route 53 latency-based routing sends each request to healthy Application Load Balancers in the lowest-latency Region; Amazon EKS clusters span Availability Zones and Regions.
DynamoDB global tables give a fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active database with fast local reads and writes.
AWS IoT Core is the broker for vehicle connectivity; IoT rules send telemetry to Amazon MSK; the MSK credentials for the rule are stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
Vehicles also batch telemetry and upload it directly to Amazon S3 using a pre-signed URL.
The vehicle's last known state is saved in DynamoDB; AWS AppSync gives the companion app a GraphQL API, and subscriptions push real-time changes because changes are small and incremental.
CloudFront routes app requests to the API in the lowest-latency Region; EventBridge enriches events; ElastiCache for Redis tracks which apps are connected.
A data mesh publishes data products in the Glue Data Catalog with Lake Formation permissions; PII is masked and anonymised and shared through secondary S3 buckets with sanitised data.

facts: Telecom data, including call data records, billing data and customer care data, is collected in an Amazon S3 bucket.

sources.title: Building AI Agents for Telecom Network Operations
facts: Amazon EventBridge streams raw alarm and KPI signals into an agent runtime hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore; Bedrock foundation models reason at each step.

Cascade detection sorts alarms by time within each site and surfaces the first root-cause candidate per site, counting the symptoms after it.
Amazon SNS delivers recommendations to the on-call engineer; with 47 alarms the agent triaged in about 20 seconds against an estimated 30+ minutes by hand.
Start with the 3 to 5 highest-volume alarm categories the operations centre handles.

sources.title: Guidance for Omni-Channel Customer Engagement for Travel & Hospitality on AWS
facts: S3 stores the website and configuration files; CloudFront serves the unified user interface.
Lambda gives guests personalised recommendations through API Gateway; Cognito controls access to the API.
A serverless DynamoDB database collects guest data from several sources.
A chatbot built with Amazon Lex V2 asks guests for input; OpenSearch Service recommends available products; Amazon Pinpoint schedules mail and push notifications.
Security: Lambda has least-privilege roles; guest data in DynamoDB is encrypted at rest.
Reliability: serverless parts scale automatically; DynamoDB cross-Region deployment is recommended for higher availability.
Performance: use DynamoDB on-demand for unexpected traffic and provisioned mode for consistent traffic; watch CloudWatch alarms and Lambda metrics.

sources.title: Guidance for Serverless Reservation System for Lodging on AWS
facts: The admin portal is stored in S3 and served by CloudFront; staff create room types, rates and rules through API Gateway, which uses Cognito to check credentials.
Lambda stores the configuration in S3 and DynamoDB, and configuration changes raise EventBridge events.
An EventBridge event starts a Lambda function that updates inventory in an Amazon Aurora Serverless database.
A geolocation service on Fargate calls Amazon Location Service; ElastiCache caches results to improve performance and cut cost.
Bookings go through API Gateway, Lambda and S3, are recorded in Amazon QLDB, and are published to Kinesis for dynamic pricing and analytics.
Aurora Serverless scales database capacity with demand; CloudTrail gives visibility into account activity.

sources.title: Guidance for Hotel Check-In Experience on AWS
facts: Guest activity arrives as events through EventBridge, or from software as a service apps through Amazon AppFlow.
Step Functions works out the guest location and journey stage, such as checking in.
Lambda and an Amazon SageMaker trained model infer the next best action.
DynamoDB stores check-in information, location and the next best action, and DynamoDB Streams triggers guest notifications.
Amazon Pinpoint tells guests about check-in and room readiness by email, text, push or in-app message; apps call an API Gateway endpoint.
Guest data in DynamoDB and S3 is encrypted at rest.
